label: Words they use · Muslim
title: Hafs, Warsh, Qalun
text: different transmitted readings of the Quran.

label: Words they use · Roman Catholic
title: Magisterium
text: the Church's teaching office (the pope and the bishops in communion with him), which alone can authentically interpret Scripture and Tradition [CCC 85, 100].

label: Words they use · Roman Catholic
title: Sacred Tradition
text: teaching handed down outside Scripture and held with "equal" reverence [CCC 82].

label: Words they use · Roman Catholic
title: Ex cathedra
text: the pope defining faith or morals "from the chair," held to be infallible and "irreformable" [Vatican I].

label: Words they use · Roman Catholic
title: Transubstantiation
text: the whole substance of bread and wine becomes Christ's body and blood, "truly, really, and substantially" [Trent, Sess. 13, can. 1; CCC 1376].

label: Words they use · Roman Catholic
title: Latria / dulia / hyperdulia
text: worship due to God alone / honor to saints / the higher honor given to Mary.

label: Words they use · Roman Catholic
title: Infused vs. imputed righteousness
text: Rome says God makes us "inwardly just" [CCC 1992]. Scripture says God credits Christ's righteousness to us (Rom 4:6; 2 Cor 5:21).

label: Words they use · Roman Catholic
title: Mortal sin
text: grave sin that destroys sanctifying grace and, if unrepented, leads to hell [CCC 1861].

label: Words they use · Roman Catholic
title: Purgatory
text: final purification after death for those who die in grace "but still imperfectly purified" [CCC 1030–1031].

label: Words they use · Roman Catholic
title: Indulgence
text: remission of temporal punishment for sins already forgiven, applicable to oneself or to souls in purgatory [CCC 1471, 1498].

label: Words they use · Roman Catholic
title: Deuterocanonical books
text: what Rome calls the Apocrypha: Tobit, Judith, Wisdom, Sirach, Baruch, 1–2 Maccabees, and additions to Esther and Daniel [Trent, Sess. 4].

label: Words they use · Roman Catholic
title: Judaizers
text: teachers in the New Testament who believed in Jesus and said Gentiles must also be circumcised and keep the Law of Moses to be saved (Acts 15:1, 5). Galatians was written against them.

label: Words they use · Roman Catholic
title: Necessary vs. sufficient
text: Rome says grace, faith and Scripture are necessary. The Reformation said each is also enough: Scripture alone, grace alone, faith alone, Christ alone.

label: Words they use · Roman Catholic
title: Unam Sanctam
text: the 1302 bull of Boniface VIII that defined submission to the Roman Pontiff as necessary for salvation.

label: Words they use · Jewish
title: Tanakh
text: The Hebrew Scriptures, our Old Testament: Torah (Law), Nevi'im (Prophets) and Ketuvim (Writings). Same books, different order.

label: Words they use · Jewish
title: Torah
text: The five books of Moses. Also used loosely for all Jewish teaching.

label: Words they use · Jewish
title: Talmud
text: The written collection of rabbinic discussion (Mishnah and Gemara), finished centuries after Jesus. Orthodox Jews treat it as the authoritative "oral Torah."

label: Words they use · Jewish
title: Mashiach
text: Messiah, "anointed one." In Judaism, a human king from David still to come.

label: Words they use · Jewish
title: Shema
text: "Hear, O Israel" (Deut 6:4), the daily confession that God is one.

label: Words they use · Jewish
title: Hashem
text: "The Name." How observant Jews refer to God rather than pronounce His name.

label: Words they use · Jewish
title: Teshuvah
text: Repentance, literally "return." With prayer and charity, the rabbinic answer to how sin is forgiven.

label: Words they use · Jewish
title: Yom Kippur
text: The Day of Atonement (Lev 16). Today kept with fasting and prayer, without the sacrifices Leviticus commands.

label: Words they use · Jewish
title: Haftarah
text: The set reading from the Prophets in synagogue each week. Isaiah 53 is not among the readings.

label: Words they use · Jewish
title: Targum
text: An ancient Aramaic paraphrase of the Hebrew Scriptures read in synagogues.

label: Words they use · Jewish
title: Rashi
text: Rabbi Shlomo Yitzchaki (died 1105), the most widely read Jewish commentator. He made "the servant is Israel" the standard reading of Isaiah 53.

label: Words they use · Jewish
title: Yeshua
text: The Hebrew name of Jesus. Jewish believers in Him often use it.

label: Words they use · Progressive Christian
title: Progressive Christianity
text: A movement that keeps Christian language while revising or dropping historic doctrine. Today's form of the theological liberalism Machen answered in 1923.

label: Words they use · Progressive Christian
title: Deconstruction
text: Taking apart the beliefs one was raised with. For some it ends in a truer faith; for many it ends in leaving the faith.

label: Words they use · Progressive Christian
title: Red-letter Christian
text: One who claims to follow Jesus' own words (printed in red in some Bibles) over the rest of Scripture.

label: Words they use · Progressive Christian
title: Penal substitution
text: Christ bore the penalty of God's wrath in the place of sinners. The heart of the gospel, and the doctrine progressives most often reject.

label: Words they use · Progressive Christian
title: "Cosmic child abuse"
text: A slogan against penal substitution, from Steve Chalke's The Lost Message of Jesus (2003).

label: Words they use · Progressive Christian
title: Universalism
text: Everyone will be saved in the end, whatever they believed.

label: Words they use · Progressive Christian
title: Affirming / inclusive
text: Approving same-sex relationships and transgender identities as good, and treating disagreement as harm.

label: Words they use · Progressive Christian
title: Social gospel
text: Salvation understood as the reform of society rather than the forgiveness of sinners.

label: Words they use · Progressive Christian
title: Lived experience / "my truth"
text: Personal experience treated as an authority that Scripture may not overrule.

label: Words they use · Oneness Pentecostal
title: Oneness
text: the teaching that God is one person who shows Himself as Father, Son and Holy Spirit, and whose name is Jesus.

label: Words they use · Oneness Pentecostal
title: Modalism (Sabellianism)
text: the ancient name for the same idea: one person in three modes or roles. The church rejected it in the third century.

label: Words they use · Oneness Pentecostal
title: Jesus' name baptism
text: baptism with the words "in the name of Jesus Christ," held to be the only valid form and necessary for forgiveness.

label: Words they use · Oneness Pentecostal
title: Initial evidence
text: speaking in tongues as the necessary first sign of receiving the Holy Spirit.

label: Words they use · Oneness Pentecostal
title: Apostolic
text: what many Oneness churches call themselves, meaning they hold the doctrine and practice of the apostles in Acts.

label: Words they use · Oneness Pentecostal
title: Manifestation
text: their word for Father, Son and Spirit, in place of "person."

label: Words they use · Oneness Pentecostal
title: UPCI
text: the United Pentecostal Church International, the largest Oneness body.

label: Words they use · Eastern Orthodox
title: Holy Tradition
text: "the doctrine of the faith, the law of God, the sacraments, and the ritual as handed down" [Philaret Q17]. It includes Scripture and the councils.

label: Words they use · Eastern Orthodox
title: Theosis (deification)
text: sharing in the life of God as the goal of salvation [GOARCH, "Spirituality"]. Not sharing God's essence.

label: Words they use · Eastern Orthodox
title: Synergy
text: God's grace and human effort working together in salvation.

label: Words they use · Eastern Orthodox
title: Theotokos
text: "God-bearer," the title for Mary affirmed at Ephesus (431).

label: Words they use · Eastern Orthodox
title: Ever-virgin
text: Mary remained a virgin before, during and after Christ's birth [Philaret Q186].

label: Words they use · Eastern Orthodox
title: Proskynesis vs. latreia
text: veneration (bowing, kissing) given to icons and saints / worship given to God alone [Nicaea II].

label: Words they use · Eastern Orthodox
title: Ancestral sin
text: we inherit death and corruption from Adam, but not his guilt [OCA Q&A, "Original Sin"].

label: Words they use · Eastern Orthodox
title: Essence / energies
text: God's unknowable essence vs. His uncreated energies, in which believers participate (Gregory Palamas).

label: Words they use · Eastern Orthodox
title: Toll houses
text: a pious tradition about demonic testing of the soul after death; not dogma.

label: Words they use · Eastern Orthodox
title: Dormition
text: Mary's "falling asleep" (Aug. 15). Many Orthodox believe she was taken bodily to heaven, but the East never defined it as Rome did in 1950.

label: Words they use · Eastern Orthodox
title: Chrismation
text: anointing with holy oil (chrism) right after baptism, the Orthodox form of confirmation. It is also how most converts from other churches are received.

label: Words they use · Eastern Orthodox
title: Infant communion
text: baptized and chrismated infants receive communion [OCA, The Orthodox Faith, vol. 2].

label: Words they use · Eastern Orthodox
title: Prayers for the departed
text: prayers, alms and the liturgy offered for the dead, which Dositheus says deliver some souls from Hades [Decree 18].

label: Words they use · Atheist
title: Atheist
text: does not believe in God. Some go further and say there is no God.

label: Words they use · Atheist
title: Agnostic
text: says they don't know, or that no one can know.

label: Words they use · Atheist
title: Naturalism
text: the view that nature is all there is.

label: Words they use · Atheist
title: Objective morality
text: right and wrong that are true whatever anyone thinks.

label: Words they use · Atheist
title: Burden of proof
text: whoever makes a claim has to back it up. "There is no God" is a claim.

label: Words they use · Words we use
title: Trinity
text: one God in three Persons. See The Trinity.

label: Words they use · Words we use
title: Two natures
text: Jesus is one Person who is truly God and truly man.

label: Words they use · Words we use
title: Ransom
text: the price that frees a captive. Scripture says no man can pay it for another and that God redeems. Jesus gave His life as the ransom.

label: Words they use · Words we use
title: Mediator
text: the one who stands between God and men. Jesus is the one mediator because He is truly God and truly man.

label: Words they use · Words we use
title: Monogenes
text: the unique, only begotten Son. It marks His unique, eternal relationship to the Father, never creation (LSB: "only begotten").

label: Words they use · Words we use
title: Prototokos
text: Greek for "firstborn." In texts like Col 1:15 (cf. Ps 89:27) it means the preeminent heir, not the first one created.

label: Words they use · Words we use
title: Arche
text: Greek for "beginning," "origin" or "ruler."
